lines: They broke on my hurdles and your bow. That's the first night held.
The library's bell used to warn the whole valley. Put it back in its cupola when the square reopens, and we'll hear the next lot coming.
My hurdles are on both pads, across the halt road. They'll hold a while. The rest is your bow.
Ring when you're ready, not before.
Their camp's still out on the halt road. I can see their eyes from the stall at dusk.
Hale's hurdles are ready whenever you are.
